change: Double the harvest period30→60 game seconds and per-tile base batch0.4→0.8, keeping per-second production and per30s economy rates unchanged. Preserve11s spoilage, staggered farms and physical collection. Protect the first harvest from premature120s inactivity.

source.comparison: Cadence-only comparison: both variants use the same frozen engine, including unrelated concurrent work. The control changes only FIELD_HARVEST_SECONDS from60 to30; batch amount and economy conversion derive from that constant. This isolates harvest cadence from concurrent forbidden-zone implementation. Wall time is diagnostic only.

controlled.methodology: Same fixed grassland fixtures, palace road ring and WASM bytes. Each variant initializes its own normal staggered harvest schedule, then runs 180 warmup seconds by default and 600 measured seconds at dt 0.1. Farms, housing and population are fixed; large food reserve prevents starvation and a negative birth accumulator prevents births. Expansion, raids and wildlife are absent. Benchmark-only recordTraffic bypass locks the road network; harvest, expiry, dispatch, movement, collision, pickup, delivery and farm inactivity use production code. Every findPath entry is counted, including JavaScript/native requests, failures and recursive fallbacks. These are pathfinder API calls, not just WASM searches. Per-step outside/moving counts measure simulated courier activity, not viewport-visible sprites or FPS. Wall time includes instrumentation and is diagnostic only.

physicalEconomyCalibration.methodology: Same frozen engine/period-only control; normal traffic road formation enabled, no WASM installation (JavaScript pathfinding),150s warmup and300s measured. Existing calibration asserts90–110 food/30s for the100-person ring fixture and a deficit for140 people caused by distance/spoilage. Both pass. These measurements include changed road formation/door choices and finite collection windows, unlike the fixed-road cadence comparison.

control.assumptions: 64x64 flat fertile grassland, no irrigation/bonuses; roads absent unless specified, 4-tile-radius urban core, farms packed around all 360 degrees. Real courier dispatch/pathfinding/speed/collection/expiry/delivery. 150s warmup then 300s measured. Population and housing growth held fixed; food reserve prevents starvation changes.

current.assumptions: 64x64 flat fertile grassland, no irrigation/bonuses; roads absent unless specified, 4-tile-radius urban core, farms packed around all 360 degrees. Real courier dispatch/pathfinding/speed/collection/expiry/delivery. 150s warmup then 300s measured. Population and housing growth held fixed; food reserve prevents starvation changes.

initialFullSuite.failure: An existing simulation test assumed delivery occurred in economy tick1. Updated it to capture the actual harvest tick while still asserting no consumption tick occurred during the delivery window.

checks: 60s harvest timing and unchanged gross production
unchanged spoilage deadlines and storage/orchard bonuses
late first-harvest grace and established120s inactivity
fixed population, farm, collector and road counts during controlled comparison

limitations: Counts describe all living outside collectors, not viewport-specific sprites or FPS.
Persistent collector entities remain one per farm; they spend more time hidden and idle.
Each scene has one deterministic control/current pair,180s warmup then600s measured atdt0.1.

Gross production rates are preserved exactly; actual delivered food depends on expiry, door choices and traffic. Fixed-road large fixture delivered1.04% less; normal-traffic calibration varies by layout.
New ordinary farms first ripen after60–120s. Larger less-frequent batches change short-term food availability and loss per courier.
Fewer trips also reduce physical road-wear entries and exposed raid targets.
No function-level CPU profile or browser FPS measurement was made for this cadence change.
